title: a block decoder wrote a full 8x8 block regardless of how much of it lay inside the tile
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a fixed-size block write at the edge of a region that is not a multiple of the block
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, no inner layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/exr.c carries `int bw = FFMIN(8, td->xsize - x);` and `int bh = FFMIN(8, td->ysize - y);` with the loops bounded by them. The unclamped `yy < 8` / `xx < 8` form is at f45da79b2c33^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **CAUGHT** at ffh_write_probe_u8+0x58 -- cause 7, a bounds violation on a store; pc=0xc020ec30, address=0xc02521d0.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc020e5b8 address=0xc0251768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image bb786221be7123f7. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102228, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_write_probe_u8 0x102210` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.

native-detect.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow at the labelled probe on the buggy arm and is silent on the fixed arm -- keyed on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string AddressSanitizer.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions. Capstone measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-capstone/): spatial CAUGHT, sublet CAUGHT.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_malloc / av_mallocz / av_calloc / av_malloc_array -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool or AVRefStructPool between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the loop steps in 8s and the BLOCK is always written whole, so the crossing appears only when the tile's dimensions are not multiples of 8 -- a property of the image rather than of any index. That is why the fix clamps with FFMIN against the tile's own xsize and ysize rather than bounding the destination.
